second_order: calling people in to build and back up the crest
theme_note: Calls recruit the subreddit to start, reinforce, or expand the shared Hogwarts image.

second_order: celebrating and checking that the crest is still there
theme_note: Participants announce, praise, inspect, and report the changing condition of the crest.

second_order: repairing and defending the crest one pixel at a time
theme_note: Participants answer damage with cleaning, tiny repairs, vigilance, and accounts used or alleged to be used for defense.

second_order: working out the crest colours and pattern
theme_note: Participants diagnose a mirrored or wrongly coloured crest, try changes, and exchange corrective patterns.

second_order: adding a snake beside the crest
theme_note: Participants propose, complete, lose, and try to remake a snake attached to the Hogwarts work.

second_order: flooding the subreddit with Snek and basilisk jokes
theme_note: After the canvas snake is destroyed, participants turn Snek and basilisk pictures into the rooms own April Fools performance.

second_order: explaining what r/place is to people asking
theme_note: Participants ask about the unfamiliar venue and answer in ordinary language.

second_order: playing house Quidditch alongside the canvas
theme_note: Participants answer the community bot, interpret double balls as double points, and award a house point while canvas work continues.

second_order: meeting the builders next door
theme_note: A neighbouring community introduces its adjacent work peacefully and shares its template.

second_order: working out borders with neighbouring art
theme_note: Participants judge distance, preserve a rainbow, identify neighbours, reassure them, and propose mutual defense while fitting art together.

second_order: posting an April Fools greeting
theme_note: A standalone greeting marks the room own April Fools conduct without yet joining the Snek performance.

second_order: helping other art when the crest is safe
theme_note: A participant shifts pixels to another tribute when the Hogwarts crest needs no immediate work.

second_order: searching for a place for a bigger crest
theme_note: Participants propose coordinates, avoid occupied colour areas, and ask for consensus on a larger design.

second_order: posting other April Fools claims and spoofs
theme_note: Participants make April Fools claims and spoofs outside the sustained Snek performance.

second_order: organising painters around images and extra accounts
theme_note: Participants concentrate a build by asking for maximum turnout, extra accounts, and adherence to a shared image.

second_order: building new pieces onto the Hogwarts picture
theme_note: Participants turn the crest into a base for a snitch, Hedwig, and other additions, correcting size, colour, and misplaced pixels as they build.

second_order: thanking the people who came to help
theme_note: Participants publicly thank named or collective helpers for their work.

second_order: telling the Battle for Hogwarts after the canvas closes
theme_note: Participants recount endurance, griefing, effort, time spent, and the defence they name the Battle for Hogwarts after placement ends.

second_order: turning border conflict into good-neighbour friendship
theme_note: After placement ends, participants apologise for earlier incursions, recount reciprocal protection, share a sidebar, and name friendship and unity as what came from the event.

second_order: claiming and teasing over the white-border idea
theme_note: One participant claims the successful border idea and another answers with affectionate teasing.
